correctness.rationale: The binomial bound \(\nu_3(\binom{3^s}{j})\ge s-\nu_3(j)\) yields an isometry \(v+3R(v)\) on each of the two regular input classes. The centered expansion at \(x=-1/2\) gives \(c_s+3^{s+2}v^2(u_s+9A_s(v))\) with \(u_s\equiv1\pmod3\). Hensel square roots produce an exact isometric coordinate change, and \(c_s\equiv7\pmod9\) separates the images. Counting quadratic residues and their roots yields every finite image count and fiber multiplicity. The 34 complete independent enumerations matched all targets/fibers, while the all-level claim rests on the proof.

value.rationale: The constrained adjacent-power difference is a natural counterpart to modular Waring power sums. The theorem gives a uniform all-prime-power-exponent classification at the ramified prime 3, an explicit two-sheet regular branch and a singular square branch, exact finite solubility tests and target multiplicities, and an exact 3-adic image density. These local obstructions can inform congruence sieves for consecutive-power equations. It is not merely a single finite experiment, a parameter rename, or a routine fixed-k quadratic computation.
